exchanges: Hi, I'm throwing my mum a surprise 60th and I could really use a sounding board.
A surprise 60th, how fun. I'm glad to help you think it through.
It's in six weeks, at our house and backyard. Around 60 people, which feels fitting.
Sixty for sixty, nice touch. Is the backyard big enough, or are you renting a tent?
Renting a tent, I think. My dad Venkat is in on it, but he's terrible at secrets.
Then maybe give him only the details he absolutely needs.
Ha, good plan. My cousin Ravi flies for Air Canada, so he's trying to swap shifts to make it. He's a pilot, his schedule is wild.
Hopefully he can make the swap. It would be a lovely surprise for her to see him.
Food is potluck style from the aunties, which is the only way, honestly.
Aunties' cooking beats any caterer. Do you know who's making what?
Aunt Kamala is bringing her biryani, which is legendary. People ask about it for months afterward.
Then the main event is sorted.
And her aunt, my great-aunt Sarojini, insists on making payasam, even though she's 84.
Good for her. A sweet from the eldest in the family feels right for a milestone.
For decor, I hired a guy named Ravi as well, which is funny. He does lights and draping for Indian weddings.
A wedding decorator for a backyard party means it'll look amazing.
His company is based in Brampton, so not too far.
Close enough that setup day won't be a hassle.
The photographer is a friend of mine, Inês. She did my graduation photos.
A friend behind the camera usually gets more relaxed, natural shots.
Mum's best friend from university, Joanne, is flying in from Perth. That's the big surprise.
Coming from Australia for this is huge. Your mum is going to be floored.
She has no idea. Joanne and I have been emailing in secret for months.
Months of secret emails, very spy-like. Where's she staying?
With our neighbour, Mrs. Kowalski, so Mum won't see her car or bags.
Clever. Mrs. Kowalski is now an accomplice.
She's thrilled to be involved, she loves drama.
Every surprise needs one of those.
Music: my brother Arjun is putting together a playlist of Mum's favourite old Hindi film songs.
That will set the mood perfectly, especially for the older guests.
He plays tabla too, so he might do a little live bit.
A live set from her son would be a highlight.
Correction on something earlier, the decorator Ravi isn't in Brampton. His company's in Mississauga, I looked at his card again.
Mississauga, thanks. Still close for setup.
Yes, still easy. Now the cake, Mum loves mango anything.
A mango cake or a mango mousse would be a hit. A local bakery could do something special.
There's a bakery called Sweet Mehak that does a mango cream cake.
That sounds perfect for her.
I'll order it next week. How do I actually get her out of the house for setup?
A pretend outing works well: a lunch or treat with someone she trusts, timed to bring her back once everything's ready.
My sister-in-law Fatou could take her to a spa. They're close.
A spa trip is easy to sell and keeps her away for a few hours.
Fatou's a nurse, so her shift schedule is tricky, but she has that Saturday off.
Lucky timing. That makes her the perfect decoy.
Okay, I think the plan is coming together.
It really is. Food, decor, music and the big reveal are all in place.

questions.message: What dish is my great-aunt contributing?
Aunt Kamala's the one doing payasam, right?
What does Fatou do for work?
What does Joanne do for a living?
Should I give a little speech, or would that be too much?
